chunks: And with this chain of narration, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Ali ibn Aqaba, from Musa an-Numayri, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

A man came to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, I love you.' He (peace be upon him) asked: 'Do you really love me?' The man said: 'By Allah, I love you.' The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'You will be with whomever you love.'
ai.seo_question: What does the Prophet mean when he says 'You will be with whomeever you love'?
ai.summary: This foundational hadith from Fadail al-Shia articulates the Shia doctrine of 'Anta ma'a man ahbabt' (You are with those you love), establishing that spiritual affinity in the afterlife is determined by the object of one's love. It underscores that sincere mahabbah is not merely an emotional state but a defining criterion for salvation and belonging to the Prophet's circle, a principle central to Shia theological identity.
